overall_summary: Performance analysis of FACTVERSE YouTube Shorts clearly indicates that astronomy, astrophysics, and speculative 'What If' planetary scenarios are driving the highest engagement, velocity, and view-per-day metrics. Specifically, topics involving extreme cosmic conditions (diamond planets, strange rain, unusual days/years) outperform psychological tricks, biology facts, and standard historical queries. Viewers heavily favor high-concept visual curiosity hooks combined with hypothetical scenarios.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like IYuce8vaU3Y ('What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?') and 8KEl0_pJ_68 ('What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?') generated the highest view counts and strong like-to-view ratios among recent uploads.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on 'What If you fell into...' hooks applied to newly discovered or extreme astronomical objects.

winning_patterns.evidence: A9Qa-RmuOr0 ('Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year') and QXuqYERlqSo ('This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!') show rapid traction and strong like ratios compared to older static biology facts.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form content focusing on planetary extremes, unusual physics laws, or alien weather systems.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos regarding songs stuck in the head (ef3ND4qiRHc, Jc04LVKNd2s) and basic memory facts (5AN7LUgqarc) accumulated low lifetime views and weak engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychological tricks and standard human-body trivia unless tied to a major high-stakes scientific mystery.

weak_patterns.evidence: Basic animal facts such as octopuses having three hearts (AXAfwrzzEdU, 1Bm0zw_qAAg) stall out quickly compared to dynamic space content.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid straightforward animal trivia and pivot animal content toward cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary anomalies.
